_doc: Manifest for the enclosure layer — the fence lines, yards and pens the town was full of and this project had no way to build. A static host cannot be globbed, which is why this file exists: the renderer fetches this manifest and then exactly the files it names, never a probe. An enclosure is NOT a structure record: it takes a perimeter rather than a footprint, it is roofless, and it carries no GLB, so it is drawn by renderers/web/js/enclosures.js from these numbers alone and needs no bake. docs/LIBERTIES.md L10 and L60 both name the missing enclosure archetype as what they are waiting for; this layer is the renderer-side half of it. Records are hand-authored where the evidence is a place (the wagon yard, the pound) and GENERATED where the evidence is only a treatment: town_dooryard_pickets.json is written by tools/generate_dooryard_pickets.py from the platted lots and the committed footprints, and tools/check.sh re-derives it byte for byte, because "which lots get a garden fence" is a rule and a rule has to be auditable. The three town_lot_line_* records are the same shape one scale up: tools/generate_lot_line_fences.py encloses the YARD of every improved platted lot from the committed lot lines and the committed footprints, and the fence type follows the traffic class data/streets/1835.json already grades each block's own streets with — board and picket in the built core, split rail on the edge blocks and the outlying lanes. Runs on those records are listed in SPATIAL order, which is a rendering requirement rather than tidiness: the renderer packs consecutive runs into one culling-sized mesh, so a shuffled file costs one draw call per fence.
coordinates: Local East-North-Up metres from data/datum.json's origin — the same frame data/streets/1835.json writes its street centrelines in, and the frame the sidecars' placement.local_e / local_n use.

enclosures.note: GROUND ONLY, NO FENCE (T-0097). The bare trodden band outside Fort Dearborn's walls. The enclosure here is the palisade itself — a committed structure with a baked GLB — so this record carries `runs: []` and rides this manifest for its ground alone, which renderers/web/js/yards.js reads off the same records the fence layer loads. Generated by tools/generate_fort_apron.py and re-derived byte for byte by tools/check.sh.

HAND-AUTHORED, and the smallest record on this layer (T-0882). A picket fence 10 ft by 8 ft round the grave of Mrs Charles Jouett, on the west verge of the road past Fort Dearborn's garrison garden. The 1830 Harrison plan letters the grave and Gurdon Hubbard, independently, calls it 'a picket-fence inclosure' — so the fence is the one thing here two sources agree on, and it is the only thing this record draws: no marker, no gate and no ground treatment inside it. Its size and every dimension of the fence are invented and graded reconstructed, at docs/LIBERTIES.md L229. The Fort Cemetery on the same sheet is a different place and is NOT on this layer: it is read and refused as fabric in data/traces/harrison_1830_fort_burial_ground.json.
